messages.author: 4c1108aaddb5744d
messages.subject: calculate mean values
parts:
Hi ggplot users,

I want to ask that how to calculate the mean value of two columns? This is the dataframe df, how to calculate the mean values of columns A and B in each row, and put the values into column D? Thanks a lot.
       A     B     C     D
r1   2.5   2.6   2.7
r2   3.2   3.3   2.6
r3   0.6   0.8   3.5
r4   1.1   2.5   1.9
r5   5.6   5.8   2.8

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: calculate mean values
parts:
Assuming DF is your data frame,

DF$D <- with(DF, (A + B)/2)

is a simple, although not unique. way to do it. Is there a related
ggplot2 question behind your query?

Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: calculate mean values
parts:
Hi:

par() is for base graphics. ggplot2 is built on grid graphics...not
the same. You also use print(p1) to print a ggplot, not show(). The
equivalent of par() can be done with the gridExtra package, but you
should tell us what you want to do first and what you've tried so far.

Dennis

It seems gridExtra is an appropriate package to handle this. 

For example, the dataset is below:
year  month  moist        temperature
2003  01       53.7875      60
2003  02       55.9037      62
2003  03       65.9075      72
2003  04       71.9154      76 
If I want to show month~moist and month~temperature on one screen, I can use grid.arrange() function
